title: Password Checker
story: You're signing up for a new gaming website and it asks you to create a password. You type in 'cat123' and it says 'Too short!' You try again with 'supermegacat123' and it says 'Strong password!' How does it know? By counting the letters!
why: Many apps check password strength by looking at length. `string.str_len` lets your program measure any string and make decisions based on how long it is.
analogy: `string.str_len` is like a tape measure for text � it tells you exactly how long your string is, one character at a time.
try_it: Test different passwords: try 'abc', 'hello123', 'my_super_secret', and a sentence with spaces. How long does each one measure? What's the shortest password that passes the check? What's the longest password you can think of?
tips: `string.str_len` counts EVERY character � letters, numbers, spaces, symbols, everything.
Store the length in a variable so you can use it multiple times without recounting.
An empty string `""` has a length of 0.
You can use the length in any comparison: `>=`, `<=`, `==`, `>`, `<`, `!=`.
common_mistakes: Trying to use `string.str_len` on a number � it only works with strings.
Forgetting that spaces count as characters: `"a b"` has a length of 3, not 2.
Comparing a string to a number directly: `password >= 8` doesn't make sense � use `string.str_len(password) >= 8`.
